rename.from: HttpClient.delete() does cannot handle a body in its request
rename.to: HttpClient.delete() cannot handle a body in its request

body: +1. The Kubernetes api accepts a body for it's delete endpoints. The swagger code-gen using code from [this PR](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-codegen/pull/6295) is failing because HttpClient delete won't accept a body.
Seems like the spec do no explicitly forbid DELETE from having a body even if most server seem to ignore it.
I need this also. Fairly easy for the maximum "safe" (ahem) URL length to be exceeded when using parameters for this.
I also just ran into this problem when I tried to migrate from the old HttpModule to the new HttpClientModule. :(

It would be great to have `body` param in `.delete()`.

We just migrated our project to `HttpClient` and for now we used:
```js
http.request('delete', url, { body: { ... } });
```
The same happen here. I need to send a body in a `DELETE` request and it is ignored.
Guys, DELETE does not have a body by design - https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/DELETE. It's a standard.

Is it a standard that it must not have a body, or that a body must not be _required?_

Supporting a body would be useful.  Apparently it's not uncommon.

I'm using POST unless/until this happens; if that's going to be the permanent recommendation, so be it.

Look at the table on that link, it says in the 1st row:

>> Request has body | No

I did.  I also looked up the spec, which is actually linked a little further down in that page:

[RFC 7231, section 4.3.5: DELETE](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.5)

specifically

> A payload within a DELETE request message has no defined semantics;
>  sending a payload body on a DELETE request might cause some existing
 > implementations to reject the request.

There seems to be some debate as to what this means exactly, but a conclusion I've seen (and agree with), is:

 - The DELETE method does not **need** to support it.
 - Likewise, there is no **prohibition** on supporting it.
 - Clients should not assume it is allowed on any given server.
 - If you support it, there are no particular rules about how.

In other words: It's up to the API.

Like I said, this is a convenience thing, and hardly critical.  But I don't see any HTTP-specification-based reason not to allow it.

@alvipeo That seems to be an error of MDN, both [XHR](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#the-send()-method) and [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-concept-request-method②①) allows it.

<sub>MDN is a wiki-like website that edits by everyone, it's not standard.</sub>

Anyway it seems that Angular let us put a body in a `DELETE` request, and since 4.3 version it didn't.
So, @alvipeo , if it's a standard, Angular was wrong before new version?

body: Do you have any updates on this?
So the issue come from this function because `DELETE` can contain a body: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6a7689d4eaca6963b5a6f3494df7fa9855505207/packages/common/http/src/request.ts#L25-L39

Ran into this, and I guess that the angular dev team decided to disallow it on `http.delete(...)` to raise some awareness to the fact that it might not be supported on some servers (aka prevent problems) and they left the "workaround" of using it with the generic version: `http.request('delete', ...`

IMO it's a difficult decision either way as young blood devs either lose time searching a bug, of might do so searching why the server is ignoring the body :P
